extracted.intended_audience: parties, representatives and practitioners involved in litigation before the Unified Patent Court (patent attorneys, IP lawyers, in-house counsel)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules of Procedure for conducting proceedings (infringement, revocation, interim, provisional measures, appeals, costs, evidence, service, fees, legal aid) before the Unified Patent Court, giving procedural requirements, timelines, content requirements and court powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 345 – (Implied) Assignment and procedural allocation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules referenced in the fee/assignment context (e.g., effect of single judge hearing on reimbursements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reimbursement of fixed and value-based fees upon withdrawal or settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Fixed and value-based fees may be reimbursed in set proportions depending on stage and circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When action heard by a single judge the liable party will be reimbursed by 25% of the fee. On withdrawal or settlement reimbursements to the party liable for Court fees: 60% if withdrawn/settled before closure of written procedure; 40% before closure of interim procedure; 20% before closure of oral procedure. Only one reimbursement per action/party applies and the larger reimbursement is used where multiple apply. Court may deny or decrease reimbursement in exceptional cases considering stage and procedural behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court powers to order payment of remainder or additional fee where partial payments or incorrect affirmations made
rubrics_metrics.description: Court may order payment of remainder of regular fee if 60% payment is disproportionate, or remainder plus additional 50% if affirmation is incorrect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order must state reasons; failure to pay additional fee within set time leads to decision by default against the party (per Rule 355).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 371 – Time periods for paying court fees
rubrics_metrics.description: When fixed and other fees must be paid, proof of payment requirements, and special rules for urgent cases and value-based fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fixed fees are paid on lodging; proof of payment provided with pleading. In urgency, representative must pay within period set by Court and filing may be deemed effective if paid within that period. Value-based fee paid per claimant's assessment; if judge-rapporteur determines higher value remaining fees due within 10 days; overpayments reimbursed. If Application for legal aid is lodged, ordinary timing rules may not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 375 – Aim and scope (Legal aid)
rubrics_metrics.description: Court may grant legal aid to ensure effective access to justice; legal aid may be granted for any UPC proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 376 – Costs eligible for legal aid
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal aid may cover court fees; costs of legal assistance and representation (pre-litigation advice, commencing/maintaining proceedings, related costs, enforcement); and other necessary costs (witnesses, experts, interpreters/translators, travel, accommodation, subsistence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject to Article 71(3) of the Agreement, legal aid may also cover costs awarded to the successful party if the applicant loses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 376A – Maximum amount to be paid for representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Caps legal aid cover for representation costs at the level of recoverable costs set by the Administrative Committee; thresholds may be defined and adapted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative Committee may define lower thresholds taking into account national costs and need to guarantee access to justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 377 – Conditions for granting legal aid
rubrics_metrics.description: Three conditions: (a) applicant economically unable (wholly/partly) to meet costs; (b) action has a reasonable prospect of success considering procedural position; (c) claimant must be entitled to bring actions under Article 47 (for claimants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative Committee may set thresholds; Court considers all relevant circumstances including importance of action and nature when action arises from trade/self-employed activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 377A – Conditions regarding the financial situation of the applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of income and assets: income defined as earnings after deductions for reasonable living expenses (disposable income); Administrative Committee defines permitted deductions and monthly instalment levels and adapts thresholds regularly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 378 – Application for legal aid (contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application may be lodged before or after proceedings; must contain applicant name, postal/electronic service addresses and authorised persons, other party details where known, action number or brief description, indication of value and costs to be covered, name of proposed representative (if representation costs requested), indication of financial resources and family situation, and if applicable a reasoned request for suspension of time limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application must be in a language of a Contracting Member State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 378A – Type of proof (documentary evidence required for legal aid)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be supported by evidence of need such as property and income declarations, a document showing personal monthly income for previous year or unemployment declaration or certificate of social welfare receipt, certificate of household composition, and any other official document proving financial situation. Documents should not be older than 3 months; further documentation or affidavit may be requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where appropriate, income certificates of other household members should be attached; applications lacking required proof are inadmissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 379 – Examination and decision (legal aid)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registry examines formal admissibility and financial conditions; applicants invited to correct deficiencies within 14 days if requirements not met; decision on the application taken by judge-rapporteur or standing judge; other party invited to submit observations before decision unless conditions clearly unmet; orders granting or refusing legal aid must state reasons; orders granting aid may specify exemptions, interim amounts, caps on representative fees, contributions by applicant, and designate the representative where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal aid may be granted only from date of receipt by the Court; interim payments and suspension of time limits may be ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 379A – Alteration of economic situation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must promptly inform the Court of any change in economic circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 380 – Withdrawal of legal aid
rubrics_metrics.description: Court may withdraw legal aid wholly or partly if economic situation changes or where the applicant misrepresented facts, made grossly negligent false statements, failed to inform the Court of considerable improvement, or is in arrears with payments beyond three months; withdrawal requires hearing the applicant and order must state reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 381 – Appeal (legal aid decisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Orders refusing or withdrawing legal aid may be appealed to the Court of Appeal within one month; appeals must satisfy Rules 377–379. Applications for legal aid to appeal are filed with the Court of Appeal and must satisfy the same Rules; assignment per Rule 345.8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 382 – Recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Where another party ordered to pay costs of an aided applicant, that party must refund to the Court sums advanced as legal aid; in event of shortfall applicant may be required to meet shortfall from damages/settlement; where legal aid withdrawn, applicant may be required to refund sums advanced.
